notes.meaning: The Lord speaks once more through the prophet Zechariah. After giving stern warnings about the sins of their ancestors, God now turns to bring His people words of comfort and hope.

God declares His intense love for Jerusalem and His covenant people. His jealousy here means a fierce, protective affection that leads Him to defend His city and bring judgment on the nations that harmed her.

The Lord promises to return to Jerusalem and make His home among His people once again. Because of His holy presence, the city and the temple hill will be known for genuine faithfulness to God rather than false worship.

God describes a picture of lasting peace, safety, and health in Jerusalem. Elderly men and women will live long lives without the fear of war, and the city streets will be full of healthy boys and girls playing freely.

The small group of returned exiles looked at their broken walls and thought such peace and prosperity was impossible. God reminds them that even when something seems too wonderful or hard for human beings, nothing is impossible for Him.

The Lord promises to gather His scattered people from every direction, east and west, and bring them safely back home. He renews His covenant with them, pledging to be their faithful God while they live upright lives before Him.

The people are urged to take courage and keep working on the temple, trusting the message spoken by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah. Before the work was taken up again, life had been full of distress, with poor crops, no real wages, dangerous roads, and bitter quarrels among neighbours.

God announces that He will no longer treat the surviving remnant with hardship as in earlier years. Instead of crop failures, He will provide gentle dews, fruitful vines, and rich harvests so that the people may enjoy quiet plenty.

Other nations had previously used the names of Judah and Israel as examples of a curse when wishing harm on others. Now God promises to rescue them so completely that their name will become an example of blessing instead.

Just as God firmly carried out His plan to discipline their ancestors when they provoked Him, so He has now firmly resolved to do good to Jerusalem. His past consistency in carrying out judgment guarantees that His promised blessings will certainly come to pass.

God tells the people how they must live in response to His kindness. They must always speak the truth to one another, give fair and peaceful rulings in the city courts, avoid scheming harm in their hearts, and reject lying under oath, because God hates all such deceit.

The Lord provides a direct answer to the question asked earlier about whether to keep fasting. The four yearly fasts that remembered the sad stages of Jerusalem's fall will be turned into joyful feasts of thanksgiving, provided the people love truth and peace.

God reveals that citizens from many cities and strong nations will travel to Jerusalem to pray and worship the Lord. Instead of holding back, they will eagerly urge one another to make haste and seek God's favour together.

differ.view: These verses are fulfilled spiritually in the church age as the gospel spreads to all nations, bringing Gentiles to worship God through Jesus Christ.
These verses look ahead to an earthly millennial reign of Christ, during which the nations will literally stream to the physical city of Jerusalem.

notes.meaning: People from all kinds of languages will take hold of a Jewish man's robe and plead to accompany him. They will do this because they have clearly seen that the true God is present with His people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian tradition, including Jerome, read the Jewish man whose hem is held as pointing directly to Jesus the Messiah, whom all nations seek for salvation.
